fr.elements: Main Residence; Solar Panel System; Access Drive; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Visibility; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders can identify it without delay, particularly under low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responding units can reach the residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so responders can move between the road and structures without interference.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to allow responders to reach and work around it.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings.
• Clear a turning or staging area near the end of the access drive so responding vehicles can reposition without backing out to the road.
• Post the address number visibly at the property entrance so it can be read from a responding vehicle traveling in either direction.
• Keep a pedestrian path clear between the main residence and the detached structure for responder foot movement.
• Trim shrubs or trees that block sightlines from the driveway entrance to the main residence and detached structure.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim branches on large trees that extend close to or over the roofline or walls of the structure.
• Remove dead branches and debris that have accumulated beneath the tree clusters near the structure.
• Clear any shrubs or low vegetation growing directly against the structure where vegetation contact is visible.
• Keep the area under large trees clear of fallen leaves, branches, and other loose plant material that can carry fire.
• Thin scattered trees where their canopies touch or nearly touch each other to break up continuous tree cover near the structure.
• Keep vegetation pulled back from the edges of all access routes so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure by preventing new shrub or tree growth from filling in those gaps.
